newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Congress takes break till June 4.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Congress takes break till June 4.

text.p: The Brazilian Congress will take next week off, leaving a second round vote on a re-election bill and further voting on proposed amendments to a civil service reform until at least June 4, officials said.

An aide to the government chief whip in the lower house, Benito Gama, said a low quorum and continuing "confusion" over claims deputies were paid to vote for re-election persuaded government leaders to drop the civil service voting Wednesday.
"It wasn't so much lack of quorum though the quorum was very low. It was the general confusion," she said.

The government tried to vote the most contentious of the proposed amendments to the civil service bill, including ones on the salary ceiling and job guarantees, on Tuesday and Wednesday but gave up rather than risk being trounced by the opposition.
Thursday next week is the Corpus Cristi holiday, making it impractical to schedule ballots.
"There's absolutely no point in scheduling anything for next week because no one will be here in Brasilia," Gama's aide said.
The Senate Wednesday night passed with a spectacular majority a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and other executive officers to seek re-election.
The second round vote on the law, seen also going the government's way, was also likely to take place on June 4, officials said.
